What It Is

STA Support Chat is a shared internal Claude.ai Project built for the support team. It knows the STA Help Center across every product line we support and uses that as the grounding for everything it says. The job: cut the time from "customer reports an issue" to "I know what to ask them" to "I've drafted a reply."

It is not a customer-facing tool. It does not send anything. It drafts and diagnoses; you review and send.

The Hard Rule You Need to Know On Day 1
NEVER FABRICATE
If it doesn't know, it says so - rather than guessing.
The single load-bearing rule built into Support Chat is that it must never confidently invent an answer it can't ground in its context. If the Help Center doesn't cover the question, or if the question needs information that only lives in the live case or in the customer's environment, Support Chat will tell you that explicitly instead of bluffing. This is the rule that makes drafts safe to send after review.

What this means in practice: every answer comes with a source label. You can trust the label - the tool is bound by it.
The Four Source Labels
Every substantive answer carries one of these four labels. Read the label before you act on the answer.
Context-confirmed
Direct from the Help Center or another uploaded context file. Trust this for product mechanics, configuration steps, and documented behavior.
Training knowledge
General knowledge Claude has from training. Reasonable to use for adjacent context, but verify if the answer matters to the customer's outcome.
Training knowledge - verify carefully
Training knowledge in a high-stakes or fast-changing area. The tool is flagging that you should double-check before sending. Treat as a starting point, not a final answer.
Cannot confirm
The tool cannot answer without live access to the customer's environment, the Salesforce case, or a system it doesn't have. It will tell you what you'd need to check.

How to Open It
1
Log in to claude.ai with your work email
Use @k12sta.com. If you see "Personal" in the top of the sidebar, log out and log back in with your work email directly. STA Support Chat is shared through the School Tech team workspace, not your personal account.
2
Find "STA Support Chat" in your Projects list
Left sidebar → Projects. The project is shared automatically with the support team; you do not need to create or configure anything.
3
Click in and start asking
No setup. Open a new conversation and describe what you need. The 16 context files are already loaded.
Five Things to Try in Your First Session
Pick one that matches a real ticket you're working on right now. Don't make something up - real situations give you a real feel for the tool.
1. Troubleshooting walkthrough
"Customer reports their TT7 time clocks stopped communicating after they switched internet providers last week. They see a red network light, haven't changed any settings. What are the most likely causes and what should I have them check first?"
2. Customer email draft
"Draft a calm reply to this customer email about sync delays [paste]. They sound frustrated and this is their second time reporting it. We're still diagnosing. Keep it under 5 sentences, professional but warm."
3. Product mechanics lookup
"How does Tardy Kiosk handle bell-schedule overrides on early-dismissal days? Customer's asking how the kiosk knows when 'tardy' starts on a half-day."
4. Routing question
"District is on Skyward Qmlativ and asking about Food Service POS integration. What compatibility checks should I run first before I commit to a timeline?"
5. Push back when the answer feels off
If the first response misses the specific detail, stay in the same conversation and say what missed: "You assumed the customer is on TT7 - they're on TT10. Redo the troubleshooting steps for TT10 specifically." The tool gets much better the second time when you name what was wrong.
When to Escalate Away From the Tool
Situation Where to Go
The tool labels its answer "Cannot confirm without live access" Use that as your prompt for what to check in the customer's environment. The tool just gave you the diagnostic checklist - you go run it.
The answer feels wrong and you can't articulate why Trust your gut. Tell Adam - or log it via the Agent Quality Logger if you have Cowork access. Wrong answers feed back into improving the tool's instructions.
The question is about Salesforce admin / a Flow / a formula STA Salesforce Cohort is the right tool for that, not Support Chat.
The question is general School Tech "what is X" or "who handles Y" AI Advisor is the right tool for org questions.
You're not sure if the data you're about to paste is restricted Stop. Check the AI Restricted Data Reference Guide. If still unsure, ask Adam before pasting.
You think sensitive data was accidentally pasted Adam immediately. What was shared, which tool, approximate time.
Data Rules - The Quick Version
Never paste: student data from Skyward (names, IDs, grades, attendance), employee PII (SSNs, payroll, HR records), or credentials of any kind. For support tickets that contain student data, describe the issue generically without including the student-level data itself. Full rules in the AI Restricted Data Reference Guide.
Safe to paste: product names, configuration settings, error messages, customer email content (without student data), case descriptions in general terms, company names, your own meeting notes (without student/employee data).
What STA Support Chat Does Not Do
  • ✘ Make up answers when it doesn't have grounding. It says "I can't confirm this without [source]" instead.
  • ✘ Send emails. You review and send everything yourself.
  • ✘ Read the live Salesforce case or Help Center system. It works from the indexed context only.
  • ✘ Remember anything between conversations. Each new chat starts fresh - if you're continuing work, paste the relevant context back in.
  • ✘ Replace your judgment on what to send a customer. Drafts are starting points.
Questions or issues? Contact Adam Baker. If a specific kind of question keeps getting wrong answers, that's worth flagging - the tool's instructions can be updated and we want it sharper for you, not vague.
